title: Mohnish Pabrai's Interview with Knowledge Inside podcast on August 19, 2026 - Episode 2

reader_summary.headline: Mohnish Pabrai shares lessons on wealth, risk, and giving from his life and mentors.
reader_summary.overview: Mohnish Pabrai explains how to build wealth by saving early and spending less than you earn. He argues that entrepreneurs minimize risk rather than taking random chances. Pabrai also discusses living simply, finding your life's calling, and using your resources to help others through education.

key_points.text: Humans do not change much after age five, so knowing people well lets you predict their behavior decades later.
key_points.evidence_quote: We don't really change between the age of five and 95.

key_points.text: Entrepreneurs do not take random risks; they carefully minimize danger by ensuring customers exist and cash is flowing before quitting their safe jobs.
key_points.evidence_quote: Entrepreneurs don't take risk. People think entrepreneurs take a lot of risk. They actually do everything in their power to minimize risk.

key_points.text: He believes giving money back to society is better than spending it, and he focuses on education to help bright students succeed.
key_points.evidence_quote: I saw so much poverty in India when I was growing up. And I also saw that education is a big equalizer.

key_points.text: He advises sixteen-year-olds to find what excites them and go all in, rather than trying to be good at everything.
key_points.evidence_quote: My advice to you as a 16-year-old would be, please try to figure out what is your calling in life.
